photos.question: A client has a new medication order for metoprolol. Which drug class do medications ending in -olol belong to?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #385!

💊 Can you name this drug class just from the ending?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Beta blockers

🧠 Rationale: Medications ending in -olol are beta blockers.

They block beta receptors, which slows the heart rate and lowers blood pressure.

ACE inhibitors end in -pril, and statins end in -statin.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Beta Blockers

💊 Examples:

🔹 Metoprolol

🔹 Atenolol

🔹 Propranolol

🔹 Carvedilol

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 High blood pressure

🔹 Angina

🔹 Heart failure and dysrhythmias

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Bradycardia

🔹 Low blood pressure

🔹 Fatigue and dizziness

🔹 Can hide signs of low blood sugar

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check apical pulse and BP before giving

✅ Hold if HR under 60 or BP low and notify provider

✅ Use caution with asthma

✅ Do not stop suddenly

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

-OLOL slows the roll: slower heart, lower pressure!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which resting heart rate is within the normal range for a healthy adult?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #386!

❤️ Do you know the normal heart rate range by heart?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 60 to 100/min

🧠 Rationale: A normal resting heart rate for an adult is 60 to 100 beats per minute.

Under 60 is bradycardia.

Over 100 is tachycardia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Adult Heart Rate

❤️ Normal Range:

🔹 60 to 100 beats per minute at rest

🔹 Athletes may be lower and still healthy

⚠️ Causes of Tachycardia:

🔹 Fever and pain

🔹 Dehydration or bleeding

🔹 Anxiety

🔹 Low oxygen

⚠️ Causes of Bradycardia:

🔹 Beta blockers or digoxin

🔹 Heart block

🔹 Increased intracranial pressure

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Count for a full minute if irregular

✅ Check the client, not just the monitor

✅ Report new changes with symptoms

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

60 to 100 keeps the heart in tune!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #VitalSigns #HeartRate #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client with acute pulmonary edema is coughing. Which sputum finding should the nurse expect?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #387!

🫁 This sputum color is a big clue for an emergency!

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Pink and frothy

🧠 Rationale: Pink, frothy sputum is a classic sign of acute pulmonary edema.

Fluid backs up from the left side of the heart and leaks into the alveoli.

Rust colored sputum points to pneumococcal pneumonia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Pulmonary Edema

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Severe shortness of breath

🔹 Crackles in the lungs

🔹 Pink, frothy sputum

🔹 Anxiety and restlessness

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Sit the client upright with legs down

✅ Give oxygen as ordered

✅ Give IV diuretics as ordered

✅ Monitor oxygen saturation and output

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 Falling oxygen saturation

🔹 Confusion or exhaustion

🔹 Low blood pressure

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Pink and frothy? Think fluid in the lungs, act fast!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which group of findings is known as the 3 Ps of diabetes?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #388!

🩸 Can you name the classic 3 Ps?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia

🧠 Rationale: High blood glucose pulls water into the urine, causing polyuria.

Fluid loss causes intense thirst, called polydipsia.

Cells cannot use glucose for energy, causing hunger, called polyphagia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hyperglycemia

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Polyuria: frequent urination

🔹 Polydipsia: extreme thirst

🔹 Polyphagia: extreme hunger

🔹 Blurred vision and fatigue

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check blood glucose

✅ Give insulin or meds as ordered

✅ Encourage fluids if allowed

✅ Check for ketones in type 1 diabetes

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 Fruity breath or deep, rapid breathing

🔹 Confusion

🔹 Glucose very high with vomiting

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Pee, drink, eat: the 3 Ps of high sugar!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Endocrine #Diabetes #Hyperglycemia #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Which finding is a sign of respiratory distress in an infant?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #389!

👶 Would you catch this early warning sign in a baby?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Nasal flaring and chest retractions

🧠 Rationale: Nasal flaring and retractions mean the infant is working hard to breathe.

Infants mainly breathe through the nose, so flaring is an early clue.

Grunting and head bobbing are also signs of distress.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Infant Respiratory Distress

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Nasal flaring

🔹 Retractions under or between the ribs

🔹 Grunting

🔹 Head bobbing

🔹 Fast breathing

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Clear the nose with gentle suction

✅ Keep the head of bed raised

✅ Give oxygen as ordered

✅ Watch oxygen saturation

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 Bluish lips or skin

🔹 Pauses in breathing

🔹 Too tired to feed

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Flare and pull? Baby's working too hard!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client is breastfeeding. Which hormone causes the milk let-down (ejection) reflex?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #390!

🤱 Prolactin or oxytocin? This one trips up so many students!

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Oxytocin

🧠 Rationale: Oxytocin causes the milk let-down (ejection) reflex.

Prolactin is the hormone that makes the milk.

Oxytocin also helps the uterus contract, which lowers bleeding after birth.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Breastfeeding Hormones

🍼 Prolactin:

🔹 Makes the milk

🔹 Rises with frequent feeding

💧 Oxytocin:

🔹 Lets the milk flow out

🔹 Helps the uterus contract

🔹 Can cause cramping during feeds

✅ Patient Teaching:

✅ Feed often, about 8 to 12 times a day

✅ Rest and drink fluids

✅ Cramping during early feeds is normal

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Prolactin PRODUCES, Oxytocin gets it OUT!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #OBNursing #Breastfeeding #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client is newly diagnosed with major depressive disorder. Which drug class is usually first-line?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #391!

🧠 Do you know the go-to medication class for depression?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — SSRIs

🧠 Rationale: SSRIs are usually the first-line treatment for depression.

They have fewer serious side effects than older drugs like MAOIs.

It can take 2 to 6 weeks to feel the full effect.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: SSRIs

💊 Examples:

🔹 Sertraline

🔹 Fluoxetine

🔹 Escitalopram

🔹 Citalopram

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Nausea and headache

🔹 Trouble sleeping

🔹 Serotonin syndrome if combined with other serotonin drugs

✅ Patient Teaching:

✅ Full effect takes several weeks

✅ Do not stop suddenly

✅ Avoid St. John's wort

✅ Report agitation, fever or tremors

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

SSRIs: Slow, Steady, Reliable, Initial choice!
